title: Trade, market and government revenue as a current concern
competency: Explain types of trade, supply and demand, perfect competition and consumer rights.

en.text: Trade is buying, selling or exchanging goods. It began as barter and grew with money. A market is where buyers and sellers meet, physically or online. Internal trade (wholesale, retail) is inside one country; external trade (import, export, entrepot) is between countries. Ethiopia's exports are mainly coffee, livestock products, oil seeds, flowers and more.

screens.title: A goat for salt
screens.ask: Long ago, a farmer swapped a goat for sacks of salt. What is this kind of trade called?
screens.after: Barter: exchanging one article for another of equal value. It was the earliest form of trade.

screens.title: Trade and markets
paras: Trade is the process of buying, selling or exchanging commodities.
The earliest form was barter. Trade arose because resources are unevenly spread.
Money made trade simpler. A market is a place where buyers and sellers meet: physical, like Merkato, or online.

children.label: Wholesale
children.info: Buying and selling in large quantities.

screens.title: Benefits and exports
paras: Trade gives more variety, more competition and lower prices, more technology, specialization, cooperation and tax revenue.
Ethiopia's exports are dominated by agricultural products.
They include coffee, livestock products (leather, live animals, meat), oil seeds, pulses, fruits, vegetables, flowers, textiles, natural gum, spices and minerals.

en.text: Price depends on supply (what sellers will sell) and demand (what buyers will buy). Where the supply and demand curves meet is market equilibrium. Surplus: supply greater than demand; shortage: demand greater than supply. In perfect competition, buyers and sellers are so many that all are price takers.

am.text: ዋጋ በአቅርቦትና በፍላጎት ይወሰናል። ሁለቱ መስመሮች የሚገናኙበት የገበያ ሚዛን ነው። በፍጹም ውድድር ሁሉም ዋጋ ተቀባዮች ናቸው።

screens.title: Sheep before the holiday
screens.ask: Before Fasika, many people want to buy sheep, but the number of sheep at the market stays the same. What happens to the price?
screens.after: Demand goes up while supply stays the same, so the price rises. Price depends on supply and demand.

screens.title: Supply and demand
paras: An exchange happens when buyers and sellers agree on a price.
Demand is the amount buyers are willing and able to buy.
Supply is the amount sellers are willing and able to sell.
The point where the supply and demand curves cross is market equilibrium.
screens.note: Surplus (excess supply): supply > demand. Shortage (excess demand): demand > supply.

screens.title: Reading the supply–demand graph
steps: Price (P) is on the vertical axis; quantity (Q) on the horizontal axis.
The supply curve slopes upward: higher price, more offered for sale.
The demand curve slopes downward: higher price, less bought.
They cross at the equilibrium point. Read P1 (equilibrium price) and Q1 (quantity).

screens.title: Competitive markets and consumers
paras: In a competitive market there are so many buyers and sellers that each has almost no effect on price.
They must accept the market price: they are price takers.
Goods are identical, people are free to enter or leave, and buyers know there are many sellers.

In a perfectly competitive market both buyers and sellers are price makers.
screens.why: They are price takers: they must accept the market price.
screens.clue: Can one seller change the price?

screens.text: A market with very many buyers and sellers, each with almost no effect on price, is
After a good harvest, the market has far more tomatoes than people want to buy. What is this, and what usually happens to the price?
screens.why: Supply greater than demand is a surplus (excess supply). Sellers lower the price to sell more.

en.text: Ethiopian consumers face supply problems: black marketing, hoarding, wrong weights, fake (duplicate) goods, expired products, poor quality and poor storage. Proclamation 685/2010 gives consumers rights: accurate information, free choice, no forced buying, respectful treatment, the right to complain and to be compensated.

Keeping goods hidden to sell later at a higher price is

screens.text: A trader's scale shows 1 kg but the sugar weighs 900 g. Which right and problem does this involve?
opts: Wrong weights; the buyer can complain and be compensated
screens.ans: Wrong weights; the buyer can complain and be compensated
screens.why: Wrong weights and measures is a supply problem. Consumers can complain to the authority and be compensated for damage.
